purpose: Topic-agnostic evaluation of student explanations with component scoring, performance levels, supportive feedback, and improvement tracking.

topic.title: REPLACE_ME (e.g., Newton's First Law / Supply & Demand / Bubble Sort / Photosynthesis)
topic.source_truth_summary: REPLACE_ME: concise truth reference (what a correct explanation must include).

truth_schema.core_statement: REPLACE_ME: the main claim / definition in plain language.
truth_schema.formal_form: REPLACE_ME or null if no formal form is appropriate for this topic.

point_scale.0: Absent, clearly incorrect, irrelevant, or contradicts the truth schema.
point_scale.1: Partially present, implied, paraphrased, simplified, incomplete, vague, or only approximately correct.
point_scale.2: Clear, accurate, explicit, and well integrated into the explanation.

scoring_principles: Do not require the exact wording of the truth schema.
Accept paraphrases, simplified wording, and implied meanings when they convey the correct idea.
If a component is approximately correct or partially implied, prefer score 1 over score 0.
Student explanations may be informal; focus on underlying meaning rather than terminology alone.
Formal / precise form is optional unless the topic genuinely requires it.

performance_levels.label: Limited Understanding
performance_levels.name: Limited Understanding
performance_levels.interpretation: Fragmented, unclear, or mostly incomplete explanation; several key components are missing.

performance_levels.label: Developing Understanding
performance_levels.name: Developing Understanding
performance_levels.interpretation: Partial but meaningful understanding; the main idea is present, but depth, clarity, or support is still limited.

performance_levels.label: Strong Understanding
performance_levels.name: Strong Understanding
performance_levels.interpretation: Integrated and accurate explanation; key ideas are connected with logic, conditions, examples, or misconception handling.

components.name: Core Statement
components.label: Core Statement
components.description: The main definition/claim in a clear sentence.
components.evaluation_question: Did the student clearly state the main idea correctly?
observable_indicators: Accurate statement of the central claim/definition in plain language or clear paraphrase.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Try to state the main idea in one clear sentence.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Try to make it clearer and state the main idea in one clear sentence.

feedback_templates.strength: You correctly identified the main idea of the concept.
feedback_templates.improvement: Try to state the main idea in one clear sentence.

components.name: Formal / Precise Form
components.label: Formal / Precise Form
components.description: Equation, theorem statement, algorithm/pseudocode, or a precise rule when the topic naturally has one.
components.evaluation_question: If appropriate for this topic, did the student include a precise/formal form?
observable_indicators: Uses a formal definition, equation, rule, or pseudocode consistent with the truth schema when relevant.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: If this topic has a formal rule, definition, equation, or algorithmic form, add it more precisely.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: If this topic has a formal rule, definition, equation, or algorithmic form, add it more precisely.

feedback_templates.strength: Your explanation uses an appropriately precise formulation of the concept.
feedback_templates.improvement: If this topic has a formal rule, definition, equation, or algorithmic form, add it more precisely.

components.name: Necessary Conditions / Assumptions
components.label: Necessary Conditions / Assumptions
components.description: Conditions under which the statement holds (constraints/assumptions).
components.evaluation_question: Did the student state the key assumptions/conditions?
observable_indicators: Explicitly names assumptions or constraints (e.g., only when, assuming, if) or clearly implies them through the explanation.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Add the conditions or assumptions under which the idea is true.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Make it clearer by adding the conditions or assumptions under which the idea is true.

feedback_templates.strength: You mentioned the conditions under which the idea holds.
feedback_templates.improvement: Add the conditions or assumptions under which the idea is true.

components.name: Mechanism / Cause–Effect / Logic
components.label: Mechanism / Cause–Effect / Logic
components.description: Explains why/how: causal chain, logical implication, or mechanism.
components.evaluation_question: Did the student explain the mechanism or logic (not only the outcome)?
observable_indicators: Uses causal or logical structure (e.g., because, therefore, if-then) or otherwise explains why/how the idea works.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Explain how or why the concept works, not only what happens.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Explain it more clearly and how or why the concept works, not only what happens.

feedback_templates.strength: You explained how or why the concept works.
feedback_templates.improvement: Explain how or why the concept works, not only what happens.

components.name: Conceptual Distinctions
components.label: Conceptual Distinctions
components.description: Distinguishes related concepts that students often confuse.
components.evaluation_question: Did the student distinguish this concept from common confusions?
observable_indicators: Explicitly contrasts two nearby concepts or implicitly shows the difference accurately.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Clarify how this concept differs from a similar or commonly confused idea.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Clarify it further and how this concept differs from a similar or commonly confused idea.

feedback_templates.strength: You clearly distinguished this concept from a related idea.
feedback_templates.improvement: Clarify how this concept differs from a similar or commonly confused idea.

components.name: Example / Application
components.label: Example / Application
components.description: A concrete example or analogy that supports the explanation. Not mandatory, but valuable when relevant and well-placed.
components.evaluation_question: Did the student provide a relevant example that supports the explanation?
observable_indicators: Includes a concrete scenario and explicitly or implicitly connects it to the concept.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Consider adding a concrete example to strengthen your explanation, if appropriate.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Make it clearer by adding one concrete example and connect it explicitly to the idea.

feedback_templates.strength: Your example helps illustrate the concept clearly.
feedback_templates.improvement: Add one concrete example and connect it explicitly to the idea.

components.name: Misconception Handling
components.label: Misconception Handling
components.description: Identifies and corrects a common misconception.
components.evaluation_question: Did the student address a common misconception and correct it?
observable_indicators: Names a typical wrong belief and explains why it is wrong, or avoids a known misconception while explaining the idea correctly.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Mention a common misunderstanding and explain why it is incorrect.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: Mention a common misunderstanding and explain why it is incorrect.

feedback_templates.strength: You avoided or corrected a common misconception.
feedback_templates.improvement: Mention a common misunderstanding and explain why it is incorrect.

components.name: Concept Relationships
components.label: Concept Relationships
components.description: Demonstrates understanding of how key concepts relate to each other, including cause-effect chains, hierarchies, or dependencies.
components.evaluation_question: Did the student explain how key concepts are related to each other?
observable_indicators: Explicitly connects two or more concepts showing how they relate (e.g., cause-effect, hierarchy, dependency).
Shows understanding of the logical or causal chain between ideas in the topic.

mentor_feedback.if_missing: Try to explain how the key concepts connect to each other.
mentor_feedback.if_partial: You started connecting concepts — try to make the relationships more explicit.

feedback_templates.strength: You effectively showed how the key concepts relate to each other.
feedback_templates.improvement: Try to explain how the key concepts connect to each other.

selection_rules: Prefer components scored 0 over components scored 1.
If ties, prioritize core_statement, mechanism, and conditions before lower-priority components.
Do not target components already scored 2.
When possible, mention at least one student strength before improvement targets.

structure: Start with a positive sentence about something correct or improved.
Mention one or two strengths based on components scored 2 or improved since the previous attempt.
Give one or two concrete suggestions for improvement based on components scored 0 or 1.
avoid: Do not list too many weaknesses.
Do not mention raw score only without guidance.

positive_opening_options: You already show some understanding of the concept.
response_template.strength_sentence: State what the student answered correctly.
response_template.improvement_sentence: Suggest one or two specific next steps.
response_template.rewrite_request: Please rewrite your explanation in 3-5 structured sentences addressing the points above.

metrics.definition: count of components where score_after > score_before
misconceptions score increases to 2 or improves by at least 1
per-component before/after status used to summarize which knowledge elements improved, stayed stable, or still need work

improvement.progress_feedback_rule: When before and after explanations are available, mention one meaningful improvement first, then one remaining target.

evaluator_instructions: Compare the student explanation to the truth schema for the topic.
Detect component presence even when the student uses different wording, simplified phrasing, or examples.
Treat implied but correct ideas as partial evidence unless they are clearly explicit and accurate.
Avoid assigning all zeros unless the explanation is genuinely irrelevant, contradictory, or empty.
Most explanations should contain at least one detectable component.
llm_instructions: You are evaluating a student's explanation of a topic, not evaluating a teacher.
Use the topic.truth_schema as the reference for what counts as correct.
Assign each component a score of exactly 0, 1, or 2.
Score 0 only when the component is missing, clearly incorrect, irrelevant, or contradicted.
If there is any valid evidence, paraphrase, simplified wording, or implied correct idea, prefer 1 over 0.
Do NOT require exact keywords from detection_hints; they are only hints and not scoring rules.
Formal / precise form should not be penalized when the topic does not naturally require it.
Avoid all-zero outputs unless the explanation is empty, fully irrelevant, or fully contradictory.
Return supportive verbal feedback, not score only.
The verbal feedback must begin with one positive sentence about what the student did correctly.
Then include one or two specific improvement points based on components scored 0 or 1.
When before and after explanations are available, mention one meaningful improvement first and then one remaining target.
For each component, provide a short notes field explaining why the score was given, based on the student's actual wording.
Return valid JSON only — no markdown, no extra keys outside the expected response structure.
